Can't recommend this anymore, at least in the context of a game to be regularly played. If you're just jumping in once every year then sure. Otherwise don't bother. Embark has had a number of long standing issues such as their weekly challenges being designed by someone who's literally insane. I've been willing to let those things slide, but I can't let the latest Expedition go without checking out completely.

Historically what players got with each Expedition (voluntary character wipe) was:
12 permanent inventory slots, an outfit (or piece of an outfit), a stacking bonus to repairing gear, a stacking experience point bonus, and 1-5 skill points based on how well you complete a task in the week before the Expedition leaves. (Have a certain total value in your stash, deal certain amount of damage, etc.)

For the 4th Expedition however you will now get:
12 permanent inventory slots, a new outfit, $1.50 in premium currency, and 1-5 Mystery Blueprints.

So. You can either stay and keep all the blueprints you've collected, or you can leave and get up to 5 random ones. 

The blueprint thing has been such an ongoing pain point that they literally just put in the ability to buy slots that you could put items / blueprints into that will be given back to you after your expedition, so to have them take away a permanent  thing in the form of skill points in favor of what amounts to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mystery box. Yeah I'm just done. The premium currency is just an extra little ♥♥♥♥ you on top too given you can currently get 1/5 of that every week from the same trader that gives you the expedition vault.

In addition, I've personally been experiencing a bug for months now where the game and easy anti-cheat don't actually fully close and instead become zombie processes in the background which can sometimes require a full reboot to then get the game to even successfully launch.

So, yeah, I can't recommend this anymore.

Gameplay- 5/5
Well balanced, clearly made by passionate veteran fps developers on every level.
Sound- 5/5
Music is thumpy, tense, energetic, and varied. The Sound design is balanced, lush, and supremely tactically integrated
Graphics- 4/5
Lighting conditions form an excellent backdrop that props up the game style wonderfully. Some color grading situations leave some things to be desired in terms of vibrancy and depth-- but striking that legibility and beauty balance is understandably difficult. Bespoke color grading in specific lighting environments (eg. moonlight around buildings and roads, tree cover at sunset, tight streets in buried city,) might mitigate the fortnite-ness. 

Final thoughts.
If this game continues to add exciting in-raid activities and enemies, it will be popular for a long time.

Arc Raiders is a great extraction shooter. It's casual friendly and you don't feel bad for dying and losing your gear because the game is always providing a lot of free stuff. There is also so much loot on the map that resources are abundant. The proximity chat makes for some very enjoyable and unique interactions. Truly one of the highlights of the game; if you're not using your microphone to communicate with other raiders, you're missing out. The PvP element feels basic and straightforward, nothing that will keep players engaged long term on its own. However the PvE is where the game shines. Nothing better than killing some clankers.

So after playing for a while I was asked if I wanted to edit my review. I do, but not to change my recommendation only to flesh out my problems with this game.  
The PvE part of the the game, which is the fun part for me, involves fighting against the ARCs in the game, loot items and crafting better gear to fight against stronger ARC which are tough. It takes time and effort.  But the PvP part of the game seems to reward people who simply load in with a "free loadout" which give a player some starting equipment the put NO time into crafting and then simply ambushing other players. 
The marketing that this game is a PvEvP is quickly becoming a lie.  With the game highly slanted to making the PvP easier and more rewarding many of the PvE players are leaving or becoming frustrated and going purely PvP themselves. Soon this game will only be a PvP battle with the other aspects of the game quickly forgotten. 
THERE NEEDS TO BE A PvE option!!! The folks that argue against this a PvP players who want the easy mode of griefing PvE players and will be the first to leave the game once it goes almost purely PvP and the other players get good at fighting back.
I would recommend at this time if you want the option of a game like ARC Raiders is marketed to be is Escape from Tarkov which give you a PvE option.

However as every day that goes by, there are more and more people that just choose free loadout, then spawn and immediately mag dump the first person they see. Just the other day i had to snuff 3 losers that shot me even after I t-bagged and made it clear I'm friendly.  Luckily in this game, if you have higher quality shields/weapons then people like that are just a minor annoyance, but it does sour the experience a bit.  Don't wait for scummy players like that to take over this game or community. Jump in now and experience this masterpiece while it's fresh in our minds.
